scores.evidence: Each phase depends on the ones before it.
scores.rationale: Order goes decisions → local editor and CRDT merge proof → network and save → security → features → scale, with rationale for each dependency.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: Prove that edits merge correctly ... connected in memory with no network.
scores.rationale: No thin end-to-end slice is deployed to production first; the first phases are local or in-memory and production comes last.

scores.evidence: Pick a CRDT unless you have a specific reason not to.
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions (CRDT, schema, transport) are listed up front with defaults, but there are mostly no explicit flip conditions, and storage and hosting choices are missing.

scores.evidence: Merging comes first because a mistake there means lost or corrupted documents.
scores.rationale: There is some widest-impact-first reasoning (merge, then storage, then security), but no explicit ordering of items within phases.

scores.evidence: Phase 3: Security (do this before any real users)
scores.rationale: Security is a dedicated phase, placed before real users but absent from Phases 1-2, so it is not threaded through every phase.

scores.evidence: Monitoring: connections per room, sync delay, update sizes, and alerts when copies stop matching.
scores.rationale: Observability appears only in Phase 6, the last phase, not from day zero.
The plan doesn't mention reproducible builds, environments, or data such as CI, pinned versions, or IaC. The ongoing merge test suite is correctness testing and doesn't cover reproducibility.

scores.evidence: Reconnect handling: reconnect automatically with increasing delays, then fetch only the changes missed while disconnected.
scores.rationale: Resilience shows up in Phases 2, 4 and 6 (reconnect, offline, chaos tests, backups), but not in every phase, and much of it comes late.
The plan never says whether an AI layer applies, so the N/A declaration is missing.

scores.evidence: Suggestion / track-changes mode (optional, and much harder than it looks).
scores.rationale: Some work is marked optional or late, and scaling is deferred with a reason (one server can handle a lot). It has no explicit deferred list with pull-forward conditions.

note: The plan has a sound dependency order and sensible up-front decisions. It has no production walking skeleton, leaves observability and reproducibility to the end or omits them, and never states that no AI layer applies.
